newsitem.title: USA: Alliance's Red Ant sale falls through.
newsitem.headline: Alliance's Red Ant sale falls through.

text.p: Bankrupt music distributor Alliance Entertainment Corp said on Thursday it scrapped the planned sale of its Red Ant Records unit after unsecured creditors objected to the price.

Alliance had announced last week that it would sell Red Ant for $625,000 to venture capital firm Wasserstein Perella, and retain a 10 percent share. Red Ant was founded last year by former MCA Music Entertainment chairman Al Teller with a reported $20 million backing from Wasserstein Perella.
At a bankruptcy Court hearing Wednesday to consider the deal, a committee of 11 unsecured creditors said the price was inadequate, according to an Alliance statement.
Court documents show the unsecured creditors include United Parcel Service, Bankers Trust New York Corp, TDK Corp and Harry Fox Agency, which licenses music.

At the hearing, Alliance said an offer of $2.2 million for Red Ant was submitted by Bust-It Records, an independent label formed by rapper MC Hammer. However, the proposal was not considered because Bust-It was unable to show that it could fund the deal, the statement added.
Alliance said Red Ant would have to seek Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection "on an expedited basis" unless it receives "an acceptable offer." An Alliance spokeswoman was unable to provide a time frame.
Alliance and 14 of its subsidiaries filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on July 14. Los Angeles-based Red Ant, along with several other units, was not included in the filing.

After founding Red Ant, Teller incorporated it into Alliance through a series of complex transactions designed to transform Alliance into a major music company. However, Alliance defaulted on its debts and sought bankruptcy protection. Teller resigned as chairman of Red Ant, but remains chairman of Alliance, which hopes to return to its core business as an independent music distributor.
